claims.text: Multiphase alloys with specific chemical-ordering tendencies will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is caused by the sequential evolution of ordered precipitates and matrix coherency.
The relevant initial state is an as-quenched multiphase alloy containing a supersaturated solid solution with the potential for chemical ordering.
Isothermal aging in the proposed temperature range promotes nucleation and growth of ordered precipitates.
The proposed transition occurs over aging temperatures of 0.3Tm to 0.6Tm and durations from minutes to hundreds of hours.
Aging evolves chemical order from short-range order to long-range order in precipitates.
The evolution of chemical order is coupled to changes in interfacial coherency and dislocation-cutting behavior.
Initial aging produces short-range order that increases yield strength while maintaining ductility.
Intermediate aging produces coherent long-range-ordered precipitates.
Coherent long-range-ordered precipitates impede dislocation motion through anti-phase-boundary formation.
Anti-phase-boundary-mediated impediment of dislocations causes an intermediate brittle transition.
Prolonged aging causes precipitate coarsening and loss of coherency.
Coarsening and loss of coherency shift dislocation behavior toward Orowan looping and restore ductility.
Ductility versus aging time will follow a U-shaped or otherwise non-monotonic curve.
The minimum in ductility will coincide with the peak-strength regime of ordered precipitates.
Conventional precipitation hardening in non-ordered alloys typically produces a monotonic strength increase followed by monotonic softening without an ordering-driven brittle intermediate stage.
The transition requires crystallographic compatibility between the matrix and ordered phases, such as L12 or B2 ordering.
The transition requires sufficient solute concentration to form ordered domains.
The transition may not occur when ordering is suppressed or when the ordered phase is inherently ductile.
No supplied evidence directly validates the proposed ordering requirements, time-temperature window, or non-monotonic behavior in a specific alloy system.
